blocks.text: How to read
This is a fan-made field guide, laid out like the paper manuals that used to come in the box. Most of it was written before the game came out, and it is careful about what it claims.

blocks.caption: Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, the two leads.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason and Lucia 01"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Every statement about how the game works carries a small label saying how well it is supported. Read the label before you rely on the sentence. Where the published sources disagree, the manual says so instead of picking a winner.
Nothing in this manual is official. Now that the game is out, items are being compared with launch reviews and guides and relabelled one by one.
Finding

blocks.caption: Vice City at dusk.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Vice City 27"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.title: Turn the page
blocks.text: Use the arrows beside the page, the left and right arrow keys, or Page Up and Page Down. On a wide window you see two pages at a time; on a narrow one, a single page.

blocks.title: Search
blocks.text: The search box at the top looks through every chapter and takes you to the page.

blocks.title: Pick up where you left off
blocks.text: The manual remembers the last page you had open. Use Continue Reading on the cover.

blocks.title: Paper or night
blocks.text: Paper View is the default. Night Reading swaps the paper for a dark page with the same layout.

blocks.title: Check the sources
blocks.text: Sources for a page are listed at its foot. The last chapter lists every source with the date it was last read.
Getting started:

What the game puts on screen, as it appeared in Rockstar's own pre-release footage. The launch reviews and guides read so far do not describe the display in detail, so these pages still rest on that footage.

blocks.caption: A shootout in an office: two bars at the top left, ammunition and the weapon at the top right.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 25:16

blocks.title: Wanted stars and Heat icons
blocks.text: Top right. Up to six stars, with a row of small red icons beneath showing what the police know. The Law Enforcement chapter covers both.

blocks.title: Ammunition and weapon
blocks.text: Under the stars: two numbers and the outline of the weapon in hand. In one firefight they read 40 and 250, then 34 and 221, then 20 and 205 as the shooting goes on.
blocks.frameAlt: Four white stars, four red icons, the numbers 40 and 250, and the outline of a rifle
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 14:12

blocks.title: Minimap
blocks.text: Bottom left: a rounded panel with buildings drawn in three dimensions, an arrow for you, a north marker on its edge, and, with a destination set, a pink route line and the distance.
blocks.frameAlt: A rounded minimap with a three-dimensional building, a pink route line and a distance of 1.86 miles
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 8:20

blocks.title: The minimap while wanted
blocks.text: During a police chase the minimap is tinted blue in some frames and red in others.
blocks.frameAlt: A blue-tinted minimap with a small fruit-bowl icon in its top-left corner
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 14:12

blocks.title: Heart bar and eye bar
blocks.text: Top left, seen only during a late shootout: a pink bar with a heart, and under it a purple bar with an eye. See the next page.

blocks.title: Prompts
blocks.text: Small prompts appear at the bottom right for what you can do at that moment. "Smoke" and "Throw" can be read in the footage.

items: ||The full button layout. Can I Play That? reports three controller presets and could not confirm button remapping, and PowerPyx's cheats guide says Up on the D-pad opens the phone. The few controls reported before launch are on the Controls & Display page.||

blocks.text: Health,
Rockstar has said that eating matters and that your body changes with what you do. Several details are still unknown.

blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 25:16 and 25:22

frames.alt: A full pink bar with a heart icon, split in two, above a full purple bar with an eye icon
frames.label: About 25:16, both full

frames.alt: The pink heart bar full and the purple eye bar about a quarter full
frames.label: About 25:22, eye bar draining

blocks.title: The bars
blocks.text: At the top left during a late shootout: a pink bar with a heart, divided into two halves by a marker, and under it a purple bar with an eye. The heart bar is full in every frame examined.
TGG, a creator who attended Rockstar's preview, reports three bars at the top left: health, stamina and Focus. The frames examined show only the two above.

blocks.title: Eating
blocks.text: Rob Nelson says eating has quite a dramatic effect on your health and gives a substantial buff.
In Famitsu's interview, read in translation, Nelson says a food buff strengthens a gauge beyond its normal maximum, and that once life falls below normal the extra is lost.

blocks.title: Where food comes from
blocks.text: In IGN's demo Jason takes a drink from the safehouse fridge. TGG reports goods being picked off a convenience store shelf and bought, an order at a drive-thru that gave a temporary boost, and a vending machine at a gym. IGN's writers saw food marked with a heart or a lightning bolt. ||PowerPyx's launch guides say convenience stores sell a healing item called Zombix and groceries for the fridge at home, and that cafes, takeout counters and street food vendors sell food that boosts stats.||

blocks.title: Stamina
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson says an energy drink strengthens the stamina gauge, that stamina drains with each movement of a workout, and that its base level rises with training.
TGG reports that in water the stamina bar becomes a lung-capacity meter.

blocks.title: Weight and muscle
blocks.text: Overeat and you put on weight. Gyms let you work out and go up in levels of muscularity or strength. Jason and Lucia can train together, which Nelson calls a two-for-one for managing their stats. ||PowerPyx's launch guide agrees on the gym: weights raise Strength, treadmills and bikes raise Cardio, and the two leads can train together at a fitness studio. The launch sources read do not mention putting on weight.||

blocks.title: The eye bar
blocks.text: The purple bar drains from full to empty in about fourteen seconds during the office shootout, from 25:10 to 25:24. In one of those frames the whole picture is tinted red.
Nelson describes an ability called Focus, which he compares to Eagle Eye and which, as TGG relays him, can slow combat down. The eye bar is probably its meter; no source read says so outright.

blocks.title: The fruit bowl
blocks.text: A small fruit-bowl icon sits in the top-left corner of the minimap in most gameplay frames. Nothing on screen or in the sources read says what it means.

items: Whether health comes back on its own. Nelson is relayed as saying only that rest affects how some attributes regenerate.
Whether sprinting drains stamina, and what happens when it runs out.

||Body armour is no longer unknown. PowerPyx's guide says it is sold in the Equipment section at Ammu-Nation, is switched on from the item wheel and adds a blue bar above health that soaks up gunfire until it is used up. Insider Gaming says armour bought there is delivered to the trunk of a car you own. Whether police car trunks hold it, as TGG was told, is not covered.||

||What food costs and how much can be carried. PowerPyx's guides name some of what exists: a healing item called Zombix and groceries at convenience stores, and stat-boosting food at cafes, takeout counters and street food vendors.||
"Adrenaline": Nelson names it during a shootout and does not explain it.

blocks.text: Jason and Lucia:
You play both. How they share the game is described by Rob Nelson in IGN's interview.

blocks.title: Switching
blocks.text: ||You can switch between Jason and Lucia. Before launch Nelson said the team kept this as open as possible, though the story sometimes rules it out. TheSixthAxis's review agrees: outside the missions that need one of them, you can switch whenever you like.||

blocks.title: The other one carries on
blocks.text: The lead you are not playing keeps a routine: sometimes at the safehouse, sometimes out. Switch seats in a car and the other drives. ||TheSixthAxis's review says switching puts you with the other lead somewhere else in the world, and that they are rarely in the middle of something when you arrive. Push Square's review says each lead has activities of their own.||

blocks.title: Safehouses
blocks.text: Nelson says safehouses are closer to the camps in Red Dead Redemption 2 than to earlier safehouses in how interactive they are. You can cut or shave your hair there; new styles need a salon or barber.

blocks.title: The relationship
blocks.text: A relationship system grows when the pair spend time together: exploring, playing pool or mini golf, kayaking, or robbing places. IGN reports that the romance is optional. Nelson says it gives no particular gameplay benefit: they stay partners in crime either way. ||TheSixthAxis's review calls it a bond that can go up or down: robbing stores, working out, texting and going out to eat raise it, and leaving your partner behind while running from the police lowers it.||

blocks.title: Your criminal profile
blocks.text: A separate system tracks what sort of criminal you are. Doing what a job needs is fair game; going beyond what is necessary, again and again, may shift the profile. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms the system and says continued unprovoked violence leads to the worst profile, which it calls Irredeemable.||

blocks.title: Busted
blocks.text: If either lead is arrested, it is "Busted" and a restart, as in earlier games.

items: ||What the criminal profile changes in the story. TheSixthAxis's review says only that profiles change some interactions. The profile names are on the Criminal Profile page.||
How the relationship affects the story.

||Saving the game: little has been published. PowerPyx's cheats guide says using a cheat switches off saving, and TheSixthAxis's review says a weapon picked up in the world is lost when you quit unless it has been stored.||

blocks.text: The phone
Nelson says money matters more in this story than in earlier games, and that at times you must go out and earn it to move the story on.
On the phone

blocks.title: Scanner
blocks.text: Hold the phone over a vehicle to learn whether it is locked, alarmed or tracked, what it is worth at a Pay n' Spray or a specialty car fence, and what registering it for yourself would cost. ||TheSixthAxis's review describes the same app in the released game: it scans a car and shows its sale value, its registration fee and whether it has a tracker or keyless entry. The review also says Pay 'n' Spray shops buy vehicles.||

blocks.title: Snapmatic
blocks.text: You follow people and can browse it. Nelson says the pair do not post, being on the run: they just lurk.

blocks.title: Rides
blocks.text: ||In IGN's demo the pair travelled by a ride app that IGN described as the game's version of Uber. PowerPyx's launch guide spells it RydeMe and says the app arrives in Chapter 2: the fare rises with distance, and $100 more skips the drive. Before that, and when no driver is free, Paradise Taxi can be called from the phone's contacts.||

blocks.title: Waypoints
blocks.text: Holding down on the D-pad is a quick way to set a waypoint.
Making money

blocks.caption: ||Ways of earning that Nelson named or showed in the interview before launch. PowerPyx's launch guides list all four in the released game: robberies of stores, banks and payday loan stores, stolen cars sold to buyers who pay more for better condition, goods sold to fences, and 39 gang operations.||
rows: Shops, banks, payday loan places; he says you can rob pretty much anything
Steal a car a fence wants and deliver it. A damaged car earns less, so it can be repaired first
A fence who will buy shows green with a dollar sign. In the demo the pair have jewelry to sell
Named among the action available in the open world

blocks.text: In translation, Nelson says cash you are carrying is at risk when you are Wasted or Busted, and is all lost if police or civilians take you down.

items: ||Prices and payouts are now reported, though only as one guide's launch-day figures. PowerPyx puts pawn shops at $1,000 to $12,000, the best jewelry stores at up to $25,000, small banks at $5,000 to $45,000 and large bank vaults at about $65,000 to $205,000, and prices the eight garages for sale at $160,000 in total.||
||Property: TheSixthAxis's review says garages are the only kind of property you can buy. Nothing in the launch sources read describes businesses or investments to own.||

blocks.text: Your criminal
The devil icon that appears during robberies, sometimes with a halo. This is the creator TGG's account of what Rob Nelson showed and told him.

blocks.title: The profiles
blocks.text: ||Before launch TGG reported four states: professional, aggressive, violent and psycho. TheSixthAxis's review of the released game names them Professional, Hardened, Violent and Irredeemable, and speaks of five profiles while naming only four, so the full set is not settled. TGG's account that you switch between states, and that it is not a marker sliding along a bar, has not been checked against a launch source.||

blocks.title: Not the honor system
blocks.text: TGG asked whether it was Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system. Nelson said it is quite different. It describes how you operate as a criminal, not how good a person you are.

blocks.title: What moves it
blocks.text: Restraint and control move it up. Shooting people you do not need to shoot moves it down. ||TheSixthAxis's review agrees on the direction: it says the worst profile, Irredeemable, comes from continued unprovoked violence.||

blocks.title: One each
blocks.text: Jason and Lucia have separate profiles, shown on the HUD and in a menu tab with their relationship status.

blocks.title: Hiding it
blocks.text: The notifications can be switched off. Your actions still count.

blocks.title: It can break
blocks.text: Pushed far enough, the icon cracks and then shatters. As Nelson described it, the bottom state can lock in for the rest of the playthrough. ||TheSixthAxis's review says the same of the released game: Irredeemable is the only profile that cannot be undone. The review does not describe the cracking icon.||

items: ||What the profile changes in the story. TheSixthAxis's review says profiles change some interactions and gives no detail.||
||How quickly it moves. On locking, TheSixthAxis's review says Irredeemable is the only profile that cannot be undone, so the others can be.||

blocks.text: Cash, bank
Where money is kept, and how stolen goods become money you can spend. From TGG's account of the preview.

blocks.title: Three figures
blocks.text: A bank balance, the cash you are carrying, and the value of loot you have not sold. Loot in a duffel bag shows as its own figure.

blocks.title: Bank it at an ATM
blocks.text: Banked money is safe; carried cash is not. Nelson told TGG that depositing cash means going to an ATM. The phone still does banking, payments and transfers.

blocks.title: Fences
blocks.text: Loot cannot be spent until a fence buys it or it is laundered. Drugs, jewelry and cars each go to a different fence. ||PowerPyx's launch guide names seven fences and says each pays different rates: Tyrone pays best for narcotics, Yasmani for jewelry and marked bills, Moses takes only cars without a tracker and Randy takes certain high-end cars. It adds that cash from banks and payday loan stores is marked and needs a tool called the Dye Pack Jammer before a fence will take it.||

blocks.title: What fences give back
blocks.text: Information, such as a safe code by text. Doing work for them unlocks more of what they can do for you. ||PowerPyx's launch guide gives one example, and it is sold, not given: once two payday loan stores have been robbed, the fence Yasmani sells tips on security vans for $10,000.||

blocks.title: Cash goals
blocks.text: At some points the story needs a certain amount before it moves on. Nelson told TGG you choose how to earn it.

blocks.title: What money buys
blocks.text: Clothes, weapons, car upgrades, garages, and registering stolen vehicles as your own. ||Launch sources back each of these: PowerPyx lists clothing stores, gun stores, mod shops and eight garages for sale, and TheSixthAxis's review says registering a car costs a fee that rises with its class.||

items: Whether the bank balance is shared between Jason and Lucia: one creator says so, and TGG is unsure when it would apply.

||Large purchases. TheSixthAxis's review says garages are the only kind of property you can buy. PowerPyx lists eight for sale through a phone app called Vice City Real Estate, from $4,000 to $40,000 each and $160,000 in all.||

blocks.text: Body, sleep
What TGG saw at a gym and was told about the safehouse. Nelson told him the story can be finished without managing any of it.

blocks.title: Sign in
blocks.text: At the gym in the demo, Jason and Lucia first signed up at the front desk. There were changing rooms and a vending machine. ||PowerPyx's launch guide says fitness studios charge a membership fee, and that there are also weights at the first home.||

blocks.title: The workout ring
blocks.text: Three exercises fill a ring and give a temporary boost. Strength work raises health; cardio helps stamina. ||PowerPyx's launch guide names the stats Strength and Cardio: weights raise Strength, treadmills and bikes raise Cardio, an unfinished workout gives no gain, and protein afterwards speeds recovery.||

blocks.title: Eat first
blocks.text: Stamina was low when Nelson went in. A coffee or an energy drink beforehand gives a stamina boost that makes the workout easier.

blocks.title: Rest shows
blocks.text: TGG relays other previews that the menu shows body fat, muscle and sleep quality, and that a lead who has not slept gets bags under the eyes.

blocks.title: Home comes with the story
blocks.text: The safehouse changes as chapters pass. Nelson told TGG you cannot buy more of them; garages are what you buy. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that garages are the only kind of property you can buy, and PowerPyx's guides speak of a first home whose meditation spot is only available in Chapter 1.||

blocks.title: Hair
blocks.text: A barber can take you from short hair straight to a longer style. At home you can only shorten it. Newer information TGG cites says hair does not grow by itself.

items: How long a boost lasts.
The length of an in-game day. TGG says only that it is longer than in Grand Theft Auto V.

blocks.text: Story and
How the story is laid out and how the two leads get on, as TGG reports it and as he relays other previews.

blocks.title: Chapters
blocks.text: The story is divided into chapters. Choices you make along the way can affect later events. ||PowerPyx's walkthrough lists a prologue and five chapters, and the trophy list has a trophy for finishing each of Chapters 1 to 4 and one for the final mission. The launch sources read do not say whether choices change later events.||

blocks.title: About 80 hours
blocks.text: TGG says Nelson's most recent playthrough took about 80 hours, with the story and some optional content. ||PowerPyx's trophy guide gives a similar figure for the released game: about 60 to 80 hours for the story with its optional missions, and about 200 hours for everything. These are the guide writer's own estimates.||

blocks.title: Dates are not booked
blocks.text: You bring Jason and Lucia together and do things; there is no planned date as in earlier games. You can also text the other lead. ||TheSixthAxis's review lists texting, working out, robbing stores and going out to eat among the things that raise the pair's bond.||

blocks.title: Romance is optional
blocks.text: Some creators were told the romance is up to you. The pair stay partners in crime either way.

blocks.title: Four levels
blocks.text: TGG relays Edge magazine's preview that closeness has four levels, built through time together.

blocks.title: Missions are not enough
blocks.text: He relays IGN's interview: doing missions together will not keep a romance going. You have to make time outside them.

items: How the relationship and the criminal profile change the ending, if there is more than one.

blocks.text: Controls and
The few controls and display options TGG reports. He watched the game being played and did not hold the controller.

blocks.title: On foot
blocks.text: Sprint is a click of the left stick. Cover is on R1. Crouching is back, and you can strafe while crouched. You can switch shoulders when aiming.

blocks.title: In a vehicle
blocks.text: The handbrake is X on PlayStation and A on Xbox. L1 and R1 are used for shooting while driving.

blocks.title: The minimap
blocks.text: A "classic" option keeps the minimap up at all times. A compass option replaces it. ||Can I Play That?, which gathered its list from reviews and streams and had not played the game, also lists an always-on minimap and a compass among the options.||

blocks.title: Cameras
blocks.text: Kill cams and the crash camera can each be switched off.

blocks.title: Photo and streaming
blocks.text: There is a photo studio mode. A streamer mode turns off copyrighted music. TGG saw no director mode.

blocks.title: Where the police are
blocks.text: A red and blue light at the edge of the screen shows the direction police are chasing you from.

items: The full button layout. ||Can I Play That? reports three controller presets and could not confirm button remapping.||

||Aim assist. TheSixthAxis's review says lock-on aiming is the default and that the settings allow free aim with aim assist switched off. Can I Play That?, which had not played the game itself, lists adjustable aim assist with separate toggles for drive-by and general shooting help.||

blocks.text: Found at launch:
What launch reviews and guides report that these pages did not cover. Each item is covered until you choose to see spoilers; fuller entries are in the Encyclopedia.

blocks.title: Fast travel by taxi
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's guide says there is no fast travel from the map itself. Paradise Taxi can be called from the phone's contacts once the first mission is done: set a destination, get in, and pay a flat $100 on top of the fare to skip the ride. The RydeMe app arrives in Chapter 2; its fare rises with distance and $100 skips the drive. PowerPyx says a taxi cannot reach Dalton Island.||

blocks.title: Cheats
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 61 cheats, which appear in the Progress menu only after the story is finished; each has its own requirement before its code works. To enter one, the guide says to open the phone with Up on the D-pad, hold L1 (LB on Xbox), press R1 (RB), then enter the code. Using a cheat switches off trophies, achievements and saving.||

blocks.title: Garages for sale
blocks.text: ||TheSixthAxis's review says garages are the only kind of property you can buy. PowerPyx lists eight one-car garages sold through a phone app called Vice City Real Estate, which arrives late in Chapter 2; prices run from $4,000 to $40,000 and $160,000 in all. Each parking spot lets one more vehicle be registered, up to 18 in all, and other garages are handed over by the story. PowerPyx says you start with one slot at Moses' garage; GTABase says three.||

blocks.title: Challenges
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 80 challenges in eight groups of ten: Combat, Criminal, Exploration, Fitness, Shopping, Sports, Survival and Vehicle. They are available from the start. The 100% checklist asks for 70, and 50 earn a trophy. According to PowerPyx's cheats guide, finishing five or all ten of a group unlocks vehicle cheats.||

blocks.title: The Progress database and the 100% checklist
blocks.text: ||The game keeps its own record of what you have found, opened from the map under Progress. PowerPyx puts it at about 3,000 things, including 557 vehicles, 196 weapons and 255 animals. PowerPyx's 100% checklist mostly asks for part of what exists, not all of it, for example 300 of 397 stunts and 15 of 18 card sets. PowerPyx says nothing the checklist counts can be missed, and estimates about 200 hours for the platinum trophy. These are one guide's launch-day figures.||

blocks.title: Gun stores and weapon lockers
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 24 gun stores and sorts their stock as Limited, Standard, Hunting or Expanded; it says Expanded stores have the widest range, including machine guns, sniper rifles and launchers. Every gun store sells weapons, ammunition, body armor and parachutes and carries one unique weapon variant. TheSixthAxis's review says weapons can be kept in weapon lockers or in vehicles you own; PowerPyx says unique variants can be collected again from an Ammu-Nation weapon locker.||

blocks.title: Body armor, parachute and equipment
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says body armor is sold in the Equipment section at Ammu-Nation, is switched on from the item wheel and adds a blue bar above health; the parachute is sold there too and shares its slot. DayOne's equipment guide lists tools the Manual does not mention: binoculars for scouting, a pry bar for sealed crates, a cut-off tool for heavy locks, a metal detector, a flashlight and headphones. PowerPyx says the Dye Pack Jammer, unlocked in Chapter 3, is needed before marked bills from banks and payday loan stores can be fenced.||

blocks.title: Fences by name
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists seven fences: Brian and Donnie in Key Lento early on, Moses and Dunk in Port Gellhorn, and Tyrone, Yasmani and Randy in Vice City. It says Tyrone pays best for narcotics, Yasmani for jewelry and marked bills, Moses takes only cars without a tracker and Randy takes certain high-end cars. Goods are dropped at a fence's container, and garages later allow drop-offs to a chosen fence. TheSixthAxis's review adds that prices follow demand.||

blocks.title: Robbery types and counts
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says the Progress menu groups robberies into 11 kinds, of which it itemises seven: convenience stores, liquor stores, fast food outlets, jewelry stores, pawn shops, payday loan stores and banks. Its counts are 35 smash 'n' grabs (20 jewelry stores and 15 pawn shops), seven payday loan stores, 22 banks of which eight have vaults, and 39 gang operations that restock after being robbed. Pawn shops open during Chapter 2, jewelry stores, small banks and payday loan stores during Chapter 3, and vaults late in Chapter 4. PowerPyx's two pages disagree on the number of stick-up stores (91 or 109).||
Found at launch:
What launch reviews and guides report that these pages did not cover. Each item is covered until you choose to see spoilers; fuller entries are in the Encyclopedia.

blocks.title: Making money, chapter by chapter
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's money guide says the quickest money is robbing the vaults of large banks, which pays up to $205,000 and brings four stars at once. Earlier on it recommends selling tracker-free cars to Moses in Chapter 2 and robbing jewelry stores in Chapter 3. The guide says saving up in Chapter 1 is pointless because that money is lost when the chapter ends. These are one guide's launch-day figures.||

blocks.title: After the story, mission rules and difficulty
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's guide says free roam continues after the story, missions cannot be replayed, and there are no difficulty settings or mission medals. On the map, story missions have pink icons with black letters, optional missions black icons with pink letters, and side tasks are purple. TheSixthAxis's review says the only outright failure in a mission is a lead dying; other setbacks are played through. PowerPyx also lists 14 strangers with side missions of their own.||

blocks.title: Aiming and camera
blocks.text: ||TheSixthAxis's review says lock-on aiming is the default and that the settings allow free aim with aim assist switched off. It says there is no full first-person view, though some guns can be aimed down their sights. Push Square's review says cover shooting is improved.||

blocks.title: Accessibility options
blocks.text: ||Can I Play That? has gathered the accessibility settings seen in reviews and streams; it had not played the game itself, so the list may be incomplete. There are no difficulty levels. Instead there are separate assists, such as a toggle that lowers enemy health and damage taken, simplified minigames, tap assist for quick-time events and an auto-drive option. It also lists a screen reader, resizable subtitles, a high contrast mode and adjustable blood and gore, and could not confirm button remapping.||

blocks.title: Performance on each console
blocks.text: ||Push Square's review, played on PlayStation 5 Pro, reports 30 frames per second with no 60 frames per second option. Pure Xbox's summary of Digital Foundry's analysis says all four consoles target 30 frames per second, ranks PlayStation 5 Pro best and says Xbox Series S is the least steady.||

blocks.title: Character stats and how to raise them
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's guide says weights raise Strength and treadmills or bikes raise Cardio, at home early on and at paid fitness studios later. It says finishing or quitting a shooting range challenge permanently raises the Focus stat, and names pool and fishing as other ways to raise Focus. An unfinished workout gives no gain, and protein afterwards speeds recovery.||

blocks.title: Launch activities: races, ranges, drones, games and sports
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx counts 40 races in six groups and 13 separate race challenges with bronze, silver and gold medals. It lists two shooting ranges with 42 gold medals between them, 42 drone time trials at 14 sites, four playable video games, three mini golf courses, 100 basketball hoops and 18 meditations. Hunting assignments from Bret Vogel can only be played as Jason, according to PowerPyx.||

blocks.title: Gangs tracked by the game
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says the Progress menu tracks nine gangs with 39 robbable operations between them. It counts them by owner: Kingfishers 3, Kolts & Associates 5, M7 2, La Polilla Negra 2, Final Chapter 4, San4San 5, PTT Youngin$ 2, The Guardia Brothers 3 and other criminals 13. A site shows a yellow icon until visited and counts as done only when every key valuable is taken.||

blocks.title: Stores and services: fuel, resprays, salons and clothing
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx counts 57 gas stations, 19 Pay 'n' Spray shops, 14 mod shops, 18 hair and beauty salons and 67 clothing stores. A Pay 'n' Spray repairs and repaints a vehicle, and from early Chapter 3 it also buys stolen vehicles and registers ones with standard trackers. PowerPyx says all salons offer the standard hairstyles and some add their own, and that beauty salons also let Lucia change nail color and makeup.||

chapters.title: Leonida & Vice City
chapters.intro: ||Before launch Rockstar named six places in the State of Leonida, listed here in its own order of billing. PowerPyx's launch guide divides the released map differently, into five main regions, and its lists use five counties: Mariana, Vice-Dale, Leonard, Kelly and Lummox.||

chapters.title: Characters
chapters.intro: Two leads and the six supporting characters named in Rockstar's published bios.

chapters.title: Vehicles
chapters.intro: ||Vehicles and vehicle types seen in official material before launch, with names only where Rockstar published them. The released game has far more: PowerPyx's guide to the Progress database counts 557 vehicles, 277 base models and 280 Standout versions.||

chapters.title: Activities
chapters.intro: ||Things to do between missions. The first entries come from Rockstar's Extended Look; launch guides have since listed races, shooting ranges, drone time trials, pool, golf, basketball, fishing, hunting, meditation and playable video games.||

blocks.text: Robberies
blocks.sub: How the pair make their money

blocks.text: Rob Nelson calls robberies a huge part of what you can, and need to, do between story missions. You can rob as Jason and Lucia together or alone.

blocks.caption: Two characters tie bandanas over their faces at a door marked Open 7 Days.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:28

blocks.text: You can rob pretty much anything.

The callout is Nelson's phrase. The targets he names are shops, banks and payday loan places, and in the demo he points at a shop that sells headphones as somewhere you could rob. ||PowerPyx's launch guides list all three in the released game: stick ups at convenience stores, liquor stores and fast food outlets, 22 banks and seven payday loan stores, plus jewelry stores, pawn shops and gang operations.||
Robbery, as the footage shows it

blocks.title: Cover your face
blocks.text: At a glass door marked Open 7 Days, both characters tie bandanas over their faces before going in.

blocks.title: Go in armed
blocks.text: In a convenience store, one of them walks the aisles while the other goes to the counter and leans over it. The display shows a pistol in hand, and a sign by the door reads "Smile, you're on camera".
blocks.frameAlt: A character walking through a convenience store towards the counter, with the wanted display at the top right
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:48

blocks.title: The police are told
blocks.text: The wanted display is already showing inside the store: two gray stars and five Heat icons, among them a camera and a pistol.

blocks.title: Get out
blocks.text: They leave by the front door. The footage cuts away before a getaway is shown.
These are short clips cut together, and the door and the store may not be the same place. They show what a robbery can look like, not a set of rules.
Safes, exits
In IGN's interview Nelson robs a pawn shop without preparing, and says what he should have done.

blocks.caption: Inside a jewelry store during a robbery in the footage.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 18:00

blocks.title: Prepare
blocks.text: Nelson says he should really be preparing, for example by putting a vehicle out front. He goes in without. ||Push Square's review of the released game makes the same point: a robbery can end without a chase if you scout the target, change outfit and pick a getaway vehicle to suit the job.||

blocks.title: Two people, two jobs
blocks.text: IGN describes Nelson, as Jason, heading to the back to look for a safe while Lucia keeps things under control by the door.

blocks.title: Open the safe
blocks.text: He finds the safe, then tracks down its combination. He also carries an explosive, which he says would damage some of the take. ||PowerPyx's launch guides describe using sticky bombs, sold at Ammu-Nation, to blow open back-room safes. They do not say whether that costs you part of the take.||

blocks.title: Leave another way
blocks.text: With police gathering at the front, he leaves by a back door.

blocks.title: The quiet way
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson describes a tool he calls a snap gun for opening a back door quietly; kicking the door in sets off the alarm. Break the security camera and you are not seen; disable the security system and the alarm stays silent, and cash can be taken from the register without anyone knowing. ||Launch sources agree on the tool: DayOne lists the Snap Gun as a lockpick that opens locked doors quietly without setting off alarms, and PowerPyx says it is unlocked in Chapter 3 and used to enter a jewelry store by the back door unseen. TheSixthAxis's review says security footage can be deleted.||

blocks.title: Masks
blocks.text: If the police were told about a masked person, taking the mask off afterwards makes you harder to recognise. Nelson's advice, in translation: get out of the car and take it off. ||DayOne's launch equipment guide says the same: a mask hides your face from the police during a crime and should come off again once you are out of sight.||

blocks.title: Sell what you took
blocks.text: A fence who will buy shows green with a dollar sign on the map. The pair have jewelry to sell him.

blocks.title: A getaway in the footage
blocks.text: After the jewelry store, two characters leave on a motorcycle, the passenger carrying a duffel bag. The stars at that moment are hollow.
blocks.frameAlt: Two characters on a motorcycle at a junction, the passenger carrying a duffel bag
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 18:06

blocks.text: TGG reports that loot is carried in duffel bags, with its value shown on screen, and that how many bags you can take depends on the vehicle. ||DayOne's launch equipment guide lists the Duffel Bag as the way valuables such as marked bills, jewelry and drugs are hauled to a drop-off.||

items: ||How much each kind of target pays is now reported by PowerPyx's launch guides, as one guide's figures: pawn shops $1,000 to $12,000, the best jewelry stores up to $25,000, payday loan stores $2,000 to $25,000, small banks $5,000 to $45,000 and large bank vaults about $65,000 to $205,000.||

||Whether a crew can be hired. On planning, PowerPyx's walkthrough groups a run of preparation missions under each of two story heists, and Push Square's review says scouting a target first can let a robbery end without a chase.||
How long police take to arrive, and what changes it. ||The one figure in the launch guides read: PowerPyx says robbing a large bank's vault brings four stars at once.||

blocks.text: Stealing
Cars are worth money to fences, and some are harder to take and to keep than others.

blocks.title: Scan it first
blocks.text: The phone's scanner tells you whether a car is locked, alarmed or tracked, and what it is worth. In the demo it reports a car as locked, with an alarm and no tracker. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms the app in the released game: it shows a car's sale value, its registration fee and whether it has a tracker or keyless entry.||
Edge, IGN and TGG give the scanner app's name as WAINK. ||PowerPyx's launch guides write it WAiNK and also use it for scanning places: the 100% checklist asks for 100 WAiNK locations.||

blocks.title: Tools
blocks.text: Nelson names a slim jim, and a key cloner for newer and luxury cars that comes later. Some parked cars cannot be taken until you have the right tool; a car with a driver in it can always be carjacked. In translation, he adds that smashing a window sets off the alarm. ||Launch guides confirm both tools: DayOne lists the Slim Jim as a quiet but slower way into locked vehicles, and PowerPyx says the Key Cloner is a phone app handed over at the start of a Chapter 3 mission, not something you buy. TheSixthAxis's review says taking a parked car can need a keyless-entry app that the story unlocks.||

blocks.title: Trackers
blocks.text: A car with what Nelson calls an advanced tracker gives its position to the police if it is driven slowly, so it has to be driven fast. ||Launch sources confirm trackers and add a distinction: PowerPyx's guide separates cars with no tracker, a standard tracker and an advanced tracker, each sold to a different buyer, and TheSixthAxis's review says a tracked car has to be re-registered at a garage or sold. Neither repeats the detail about driving fast.||

blocks.title: Taking one that is occupied
blocks.text: You can aim your weapon and tell people to get out of their car, without having to pull anybody out. ||TheSixthAxis's review says carjacking still works but draws the police.||
The footage shows it: a masked character aims a pistol at the driver of a car, and a second character then goes to the driver's door.

blocks.caption: A masked character aims a pistol at an occupied car.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:37

blocks.title: Deliver it in good condition
blocks.text: A car fence pays less for a damaged car. Nelson says he can repair the car first. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it: buyers pay more the better the condition, with a bonus for a car delivered in mint condition. PowerPyx puts a wish-list car in perfect condition at $30,000 or more.||

blocks.title: Keep it
blocks.text: The scanner also shows what it would cost to register a car as your own. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms the fee is shown and says it rises with the class of car.||

blocks.title: Your own car
blocks.text: Your personal vehicle can be called to you, and spare outfits can be kept in its trunk. ||TheSixthAxis's review says a registered car can be called up even when it has been impounded, and Push Square's mentions a delivery service that brings a chosen car to you. Neither mentions outfits in the trunk.||

items: ||Which cars fences want is now reported. PowerPyx's launch guides say Moses buys cars with no tracker for $1,000 or more, any Pay 'n' Spray buys cars with a standard tracker for around $4,000 from Chapter 3, and Randy pays $30,000 or more for each of the 18 sports cars on his list in perfect condition.||

blocks.text: Guns
Killing is one option among several, and what you carry is on show.

blocks.caption: A shootout in a dark office, with both bars on screen at the top left.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 25:16

blocks.title: More than one way to end it
blocks.text: Nelson says a situation can be handled by threatening, knocking someone out, shooting to incapacitate, or killing. In his demo, aiming a gun without firing made the people he had angered run. ||Push Square's review of the released game says enemies can be put down by shots to non-vital areas.||

blocks.title: The yellow X
blocks.text: A yellow X when you hit someone means they are down and will not get back up.
TGG reports three hit markers: white for a hit, yellow for incapacitated, red for a kill.

blocks.title: Long guns show
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson says long guns can no longer be hidden. One on your back draws little reaction; one in your hands makes people leave or turn hostile, and the police warn you first. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it for the released game: everything you carry is visible on the character, and police grow suspicious of long guns.||

blocks.title: Where your guns are kept
blocks.text: Nelson says every weapon you have bought is always available in the back of your personal vehicle. In translation, he adds that Ammu-Nation has lockers where your guns can be collected. ||TheSixthAxis's review agrees: weapons can be kept in weapon lockers or in vehicles you own. PowerPyx's guides place the lockers at Ammu-Nation.||

blocks.title: Firing to frighten
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson describes shooting near a person, not at them, to frighten or confuse them and buy time to get away.

blocks.title: Focus
blocks.text: Nelson compares Focus to Eagle Eye. TGG relays him as saying it can slow combat down. ||TheSixthAxis's review says Focus works throughout the released game: it highlights valuables, shows enemies in nearby rooms and reveals weak spots in a fight. Push Square's review describes a bullet-time mechanic.||

items: Cover, beyond the fact that it exists. ||Push Square's review says only that cover shooting is improved.||

||Silenced weapons. Melee weapons and explosives are confirmed: TheSixthAxis's review says each lead carries one melee weapon and explosives, PowerPyx's guide to the Progress database counts 9 melee weapons and 4 explosives, and its guides describe sticky bombs sold at Ammu-Nation. TheSixthAxis's review says accessories change a gun's damage and range figures; no launch source read names a silencer.||

blocks.text: Robbery
More on robbing stores, from TGG's account of the preview and the other previews he relays.

blocks.title: Any store
blocks.text: Nelson told TGG you can try to rob any store you walk into. Small ones show no robbery icon; bigger targets can show their potential take on the map.

blocks.title: Finding the code
blocks.text: A fence may text you a safe's code, or it may be somewhere in the store. In the demo Nelson searched a back room for one.

blocks.title: Heroes
blocks.text: Customers and staff may rush you, try to take your gun, or draw their own. TGG saw both happen.

blocks.title: Cameras
blocks.text: Nelson showed him that camera recordings can be destroyed. TGG relays another preview of a shop that kept its footage in the cloud. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that security footage can be deleted.||

blocks.title: Bags and vehicles
blocks.text: Loot goes into duffel bags, and there is a limit to how many you can take. A bike gets away fast; a van carries more.

blocks.title: Other people's robberies
blocks.text: He relays previews in which masked robbers had crashed and spilled their loot, and two robbers were trapped in a jewelry store.

items: How large the bag limit is for each vehicle.

blocks.text: Tools, trackers
Getting into a car, starting it, and keeping it. TGG reports what Rob Nelson showed and told him.

blocks.title: The slim jim
blocks.text: For older cars. You work the lock with the analog sticks, and it gets you in without setting off the alarm. ||DayOne's launch equipment guide describes the Slim Jim the same way: a quiet way into locked vehicles, slower than force.||

blocks.title: The key cloner
blocks.text: Some cars cannot be hot-wired. Without a key or a cloner you can sit in one and go nowhere.

blocks.title: Occupied cars
blocks.text: A driver can resist, as a quick-time interaction. TGG watched a passenger throw Nelson back out.

blocks.title: Tracker levels
blocks.text: A fence removes trackers, but only the levels you have unlocked with him. A high-end tracker beeps faster as you slow down, then alerts the police. ||PowerPyx's launch guides describe the same ladder from the selling side: Moses takes only cars with no tracker, Pay 'n' Spray shops buy and register cars with a standard tracker from Chapter 3, and Randy takes wish-list cars with advanced trackers once you have the Key Cloner.||

blocks.title: Randy
blocks.text: ||TGG named one vehicle fence as Randy. He keeps a list of cars he wants, and tools come from progressing with contacts like him. PowerPyx's launch guides confirm him: Randy is a fence in Vice City who takes certain high-end cars, his list has 18 sports cars, and the Key Cloner arrives with a job done for him.||

blocks.title: Garages
blocks.text: A stolen car can be registered and stored. More garages can be bought; you keep as many cars as you have spaces. An app brings your car to you. ||Launch sources confirm each part: PowerPyx lists eight garages for sale through the Vice City Real Estate app and says each parking spot lets one more vehicle be registered, up to 18 in all, and Push Square's review mentions a delivery service that brings a chosen car to you.||

items: ||What each tool costs. On timing, PowerPyx's launch guides say the Key Cloner is handed over at the start of a Chapter 3 mission and is not bought, and that the Snap Gun and the Dye Pack Jammer are also unlocked through Chapter 3 jobs.||

blocks.text: Driving, fuel
How cars handle and how else you get around, as TGG reports it. He did not drive himself.

blocks.title: Weight
blocks.text: Nelson told him the team kept the best of Grand Theft Auto IV's feel with Grand Theft Auto V's accessibility. In the demo a muscle car spun out under hard acceleration.

blocks.title: Off-road
blocks.text: Fast cars and bikes reach higher top speeds than before. A supercar handles badly off the road.

blocks.title: Fuel
blocks.text: Cars need fuel. A gas station offers a repair or a fill; you hold R2 while the character fills up. Electric vehicles can be charged. ||PowerPyx's launch guide confirms fuel: it counts 57 gas stations, says every vehicle burns fuel and stops when the tank is empty, and says nearby stations are flagged on the map when fuel runs low. It does not cover charging or the controls.||

blocks.title: Mod shops
blocks.text: No single shop does everything. Each has a speciality, such as off-road builds or lowriders. ||PowerPyx's launch guide confirms it: it lists 14 mod shops, each tied to one kind of vehicle, for example retro cars, muscle cars or sports bikes.||

blocks.title: Your partner drives
blocks.text: You can swap between driver and passenger in a free-roam chase, and tell a partner at the wheel to hurry.

blocks.title: Buses and rides
blocks.text: You can take a bus or a ride and skip the journey. TGG relays Edge magazine's preview that buses keep to routes and times. ||PowerPyx's launch guide confirms the ride: a Paradise Taxi or a RydeMe car will skip the trip for $100, and there is no fast travel from the map itself. The launch entries read do not cover buses.||

items: Whether an overturned car can be rocked back onto its wheels: one creator says not, and TGG could not check.

blocks.text: Carrying and
What fits on the weapon wheel and how a fight plays, from TGG's account of the preview.

blocks.title: Two and two
blocks.text: Two handguns and two long guns. One long gun goes on your back; a second stays in your hands, where people can see it. ||TheSixthAxis's review gives the full loadout for the released game: two sidearms, two long guns, explosives, one melee weapon and equipment, all of it visible on the character.||

blocks.title: Kept and lost
blocks.text: Your loadout stays with your personal vehicle. Weapons you bought can be recovered. Ones you only picked up can be gone for good. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it: weapons can be kept in weapon lockers or in vehicles you own, and a weapon picked up in the world is lost when you quit unless it has been stored.||

blocks.title: The rest of the wheel
blocks.text: Melee weapons, gadgets and throwables have their own room, and items such as healing have a separate tab. ||TheSixthAxis's review lists explosives, one melee weapon and equipment alongside the guns. PowerPyx's guides speak of a weapon wheel, where binoculars are picked, and an item wheel, where body armor is switched on.||

blocks.title: Focus in a fight
blocks.text: Aim at a red area for a lethal shot or a yellow one to incapacitate. You still aim and fire yourself. ||TheSixthAxis's review says Focus reveals weak spots in a fight.||

blocks.title: Recoil
blocks.text: Automatic weapons kick: Nelson fired in short bursts. Pistols fire faster than in Grand Theft Auto V.

blocks.title: Hand to hand
blocks.text: Blocking, dodging and grappling. TGG relays other previews that a block can be held or a parry timed.

items: ||Ammunition: how much can be carried. PowerPyx's launch guide says every gun store sells it.||

blocks.text: Law

Law enforcement in Leonida is about more than outrunning the officer behind you. Rockstar describes police who keep hold of what they have learned about a suspect, so it matters what they know, not only whether they can see you.

blocks.caption: Jason on a motorcycle, a police vehicle close behind.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason Duval 11"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Losing sight of the police is not necessarily the same as losing their information.
Stars and Heat at a glance

Two things sit at the top right of the screen: up to six wanted stars, and beneath them a row of small red Heat icons. The stars are the wanted level. The icons are separate, and change while the stars stay the same.

blocks.credit: Frames from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:48 and 14:12

frames.alt: Two gray stars above five red icons: a camera, two heads, a coat hanger, a head and a pistol
frames.label: Camera, two heads, coat hanger, head, pistol

frames.alt: Four white stars above four red icons: two heads, a coat hanger, a head and a car
frames.label: Two heads, coat hanger, head, car

blocks.text: Rob Nelson says the icons show what the police know about you. In his demo they knew what he looked like, what he was wearing, what the pair were driving, and that they were a couple. A crime has to be seen by a witness, or set off an alarm, before it is reported at all. ||TheSixthAxis's review describes the released game the same way: witnesses can call the police, the police work from a description of you, and they know whether you are working alone or as a pair.||

blocks.caption: ||What the police know, and what to do about it, are from Nelson's interview, and TheSixthAxis's review confirms that changing your looks, clothing and vehicle stops you matching the description. Matching each to an icon is still this manual's reading of the footage, not a Rockstar statement.||
rows: Change your appearance: glasses, a hat, a haircut
Put on a different outfit, bought at a store or kept in your own car's trunk
Get out and take a different vehicle

blocks.caption: ||These two icons are in the footage. No source read names them, but TheSixthAxis's review supports the reading: it says security footage can be deleted and that weapons, like vehicles and clothing, can be changed or abandoned so you no longer match the description.||
rows: You were caught on a security camera
The police know which weapon was used

blocks.text: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson calls the mechanic the heat system, and describes police dispatch as very specific about what it knows.

The creator TGG, who previewed the game, quotes Nelson as saying the team wanted police to stop forgetting you the moment you lose them and to have "a bit more persistent memory." The quote comes from TGG's video, as reported by GamesRadar+; it is not in IGN's transcript.
||This chapter was written before release. Launch reviews and guides have since confirmed its outline, but the ones read give no timers, distances or thresholds, and none are given here.||
The wanted

blocks.caption: Four stars lit, top right, as a character fires a rifle at a police pickup.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 14:08

blocks.text: The wanted display sits at the top right of the screen and has six positions. Unlit positions show as dim placeholders, and in every frame examined the lit stars are the right-most ones. Two and four stars are lit at different times.

Playing the demo, Rob Nelson described one star as not a big deal: leave the area the police are responding to and you should generally be fine. He also said things escalate if you choose to escalate them.
When the stars are hollow, the police are responding without knowing who you are, and leaving the area is enough.
What is known, level by level

blocks.caption: Only these two levels are described by Rockstar in the sources read.
rows: Not a big deal. Leave the area the police are responding to and you should generally be fine
Hard to get away by car. He suggests getting out and going on foot through the alleys

blocks.text: In the frames examined, two stars and four stars are the only counts seen lit. No frame shows one, three, five or six stars lit.
In one moment of footage the car icon disappears as the characters leave their car, while four red stars stay lit.

||What it takes to reach each star has still not been published in full. The one figure in the launch guides read is PowerPyx's: robbing a large bank's vault brings four stars at once. Treat any fuller table of "this crime equals that many stars" as a guess until it has been tested.||

blocks.title: How the footage was read
items: Every picture of the wanted display in this chapter is a frame from Rockstar's own Extended Look, downloaded from Rockstar's media page.
The video was examined as still frames, a few seconds apart. Times are approximate, and anything that lasts less than a few seconds, or that only shows in motion, may have been missed.

blocks.title: About the pictures
items: The large photographs in this chapter are official Rockstar screenshots chosen for their subject. They are not evidence for the rule printed beside them.
The small pictures of the wanted stars and Heat icons are different: they are frames from Rockstar's Extended Look, and the claims labelled R★ Verified rest on them.

blocks.text: The stars
Four different looks appear in Rockstar's footage. What each is seen alongside is recorded here. Rockstar has described the meaning of only one of them.

blocks.title: Hollow stars
blocks.frameAlt: Two outlined stars at the right of six positions, with no icons beneath
blocks.text: About 18:04 to 18:11. Two outlined stars with dark centres and no Heat icons, as two masked characters get onto a motorcycle across the road from a jewellers. A few seconds earlier, inside a jewelry store, a camera icon shows on its own with no stars.
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 18:08

blocks.text: In his own demo, Nelson said hollow white stars mean the police do not know who you are: they head for the scene without a description, and leaving the area is enough. The outlined stars in this frame appear to be the same thing.

blocks.title: Gray stars

blocks.text: TGG says red stars mean you have lost the officers chasing you but are still inside the area being searched: the police know who they are looking for, but not where you are.
Two GamesRadar+ writers, each reading the footage for themselves, arrive at much the same meaning; one of them writes "presumably". Rockstar has not stated it in the sources read.

Two solid white stars also appear later, at about 18:24 to 18:44, first with three icons and then with four. After the hollow stars at about 18:12, some twelve seconds of footage show no display at all, so a change from hollow to solid is not seen.

blocks.text: How police
A response starts with somebody, or something, raising the alarm.

blocks.caption: Two masked people with guns at a counter while three others raise their hands.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason and Lucia 15"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.title: A witness
blocks.text: Nelson has said the wanted system needs someone to witness the crime for it to be reported. In his demo, a bystander called an incident in. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that witnesses can call the police.||

blocks.title: An alarm
blocks.text: The other route he names is an alarm being set off.

blocks.title: A vehicle tracker
blocks.text: Some cars carry what Nelson calls an advanced tracker, shown by a blinking red light. It tells the police where the car is if it is not driven fast enough. A scanner on the in-game phone can tell you beforehand whether a car is locked, alarmed or tracked.

blocks.caption: Interpretation: a simplified model for explanation, not a verified description of how the game works inside.
steps: It is witnessed, or an alarm or tracker is tripped
Police try to identify and find the suspect

blocks.title: Do not read too much into this
items: Nelson was describing the open world. Missions and scripted events may behave differently.
Being noticed is not the same as being identified: see the next pages.

blocks.text: Heat:
Heat is the information the police hold about you. On screen it appears as small icons with the wanted stars.

blocks.caption: Lucia, with a patrol officer and police lights behind her.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Lucia Caminos 14"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Nelson points to icons on screen that show what the police know. In his demo they knew what he looked like, what he was wearing, what the pair were driving, and that they were a couple. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that the police work from a description of you and know whether you are alone or a pair.||
In the footage the icons are small red discs in a row beneath the stars. Six different ones appear: a camera, two heads, a coat hanger, a single head, a pistol and a car. Up to five show at once.

blocks.caption: Five Heat icons beneath two gray stars: camera, two heads, coat hanger, head and pistol.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:48

blocks.text: One guide says the more icons are active, the harder the police are to lose.

blocks.title: Appearance
blocks.text: The police know what you look like. Glasses, a hat or a new haircut change your appearance, but not what you are wearing. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it: you can change how you look so that you no longer match the description, and hats, sunglasses and masks can hide your face during a crime.||

blocks.title: Clothing
blocks.text: The police know your outfit. Nelson calls an outfit they have seen compromised. ||TheSixthAxis's review lists clothing among the things you can change or abandon to stop matching the description.||

blocks.title: Vehicle
blocks.text: The police know what you are driving. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that changing or abandoning the vehicle is one way to stop matching the description, and PowerPyx's guide says a Pay 'n' Spray repaints a vehicle so the police no longer recognise it.||
Evidence that can

blocks.text: The police can know that Jason and Lucia are together. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that the police know whether you are working alone or as a pair.||

blocks.text: A pistol icon appears among the Heat icons at about 11:48.

||Guides read the pistol icon as the police knowing which weapon was used. Rockstar has not described it in the sources read, but TheSixthAxis's review lists weapons among the things you can change or abandon so that you no longer match the description.||

blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 18:02
blocks.text: A camera icon appears on its own, with no stars, inside a jewelry store at about 18:01 to 18:03; it is gone when the stars appear a second later. It also appears among five icons at 11:48.

||Guides and creators read the camera icon as being caught on security camera. Rockstar has not described it in the sources read, but TheSixthAxis's review says security footage can be deleted as one way of getting away.||
Several icons can be active at once, and the set changes while the stars are showing. Whether there are more than these six is not known.
Heat can rise as well as fall: in the demo, putting a bystander out of action raised it.

blocks.text: Nelson uses "heat" in two ways: for what the police know about you, and for the police searching an area ("we have heat now"). This manual keeps the two apart, but the game may not.
The two can come apart. At one point in the demo Nelson notes that the pair have got away with no heat; shortly after, police searching the area means they have heat again.
GamesRadar+, reporting the creator TGG's preview, says clues can still get you recognised later, even after the wanted stars have gone.
Finding
You are expected to look for the police, not read them off the map.

blocks.caption: Jason behind a chain-link fence with a pistol raised, as an armed figure approaches under police lights.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason Duval 07"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Nelson describes Focus as much like Eagle Eye in Red Dead Redemption 2: a way to locate things you want to find, and certainly police. In IGN's account of the demo it made a nearby officer glow.

TGG also quotes Nelson as saying that police do not show up on the radar and do show up when you use Focus, and that this is harder but more fun, depending on the wanted level. Again this is TGG's account, reported by GamesRadar+.
That Focus shows police through walls is TGG's own description, not a Nelson quote. ||TheSixthAxis's review says Focus shows enemies in nearby rooms; it does not mention police specifically.||
One guide, reading the footage, suggests that at higher wanted levels the minimap is washed out by red and blue flashing light.

blocks.text: Hot
Getting away from the scene may not make the scene safe to come back to.

blocks.caption: Patrol cars gathered on a bridge, a boat with flashing lights below and a helicopter sweeping a searchlight overhead.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Vice City 17"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Checking the map in his demo, Nelson calls the place of an incident a hot area: the police are there and will hang around for a while, and the map still shows a star over it. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that after an escape the wanted area stays marked on the map for a while.||

VICE, relaying creators' previews, calls it the active search area and says red stars mean you have escaped the chase but are still inside it. One guide describes a red zone with a lighter ring around it. What the game itself calls the area on screen is not confirmed.

blocks.title: Leave
blocks.text: At a low wanted level, getting out of the area the police are responding to is described as enough.

blocks.title: Wait
blocks.text: With police searching an area, one option Nelson lists is to wait for it to die down.

blocks.title: Coming back too soon
blocks.text: Nelson says that if you go back, the police will still be hanging around for a while.
One creator says he was told that at the highest wanted level the search covers the whole map. Treat this as hearsay until tested.

blocks.text: With three stars in the city, Nelson says getting away by car can be hard unless it is very fast, and that the best option is usually to get off the streets and go on foot through the alleys.

In the Extended Look the car icon is present at about 15:56, when the car has stopped in a garage bay with its door open, and is gone three seconds later, when the character is on foot beside it. The stars are red throughout. This is one moment of footage, not a stated rule.

blocks.title: They go to the scene
blocks.text: Without a description, police head for where the crime happened. In the demo's store robbery, Nelson expects officers to gather out front, and leaves by a back door.

blocks.title: You can stand and fight
blocks.text: Nelson says you can stay and fight the police if you want to.

blocks.title: Chases in missions
blocks.text: Where a mission turns into a chase or a robbery, Rockstar says it tries to keep it consistent with how those systems work in the open world. Your partner can drive while you deal with pursuers.

blocks.title: Patrol car equipment
blocks.text: One creator believes police cars carry shotguns or rifles in the trunk, sometimes body armor, and a tracker. VICE relays this; it is not confirmed.

blocks.title: Cars, a boat and a helicopter
blocks.text: One official screenshot shows patrol cars on a bridge, a boat with flashing police lights on the water below and a helicopter sweeping a searchlight. What brings each of them, and at which wanted level, is not known.

blocks.text: Escaping:
Details of the chase that the creator TGG reports from the preview. None has been stated by Rockstar in writing.

blocks.title: Flashing stars
blocks.text: Solid white stars mean the police can see you. Break their line of sight and the stars flash white. Red means you have escaped the chase but are still where you can be recognised.

blocks.title: Two circles
blocks.text: On the map, a darker red search area sits inside a lighter one. Getting outside both helps, and you can also hide inside them.

blocks.title: The perimeter
blocks.text: When Nelson abandoned a robbery, TGG watched police set up a perimeter outside the store.

blocks.title: Six stars
blocks.text: Nelson told TGG that at six stars the police search the whole map. Rockstar would not say what else happens.

blocks.title: Ways out
blocks.text: A respray removes the description of your car. Underwater, the depth and clarity of the water affect whether police see you. ||PowerPyx's launch guide confirms the respray: a Pay 'n' Spray repairs a vehicle and repaints it so the police no longer recognise it. The underwater detail is not covered.||

blocks.title: Dogs and spikes
blocks.text: TGG relays Edge magazine's preview: a spike strip stopped Jason's motorbike and a police dog pinned him down.

items: Whether a prison sequence exists. TGG says Nelson described a busted screen and a respawn.
